newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul panel proposes raising bank ownership limit.
newsitem.headline: Seoul panel proposes raising bank ownership limit.

text.p: A financial reform panel will propose lifting the individual shareholding limit in banks to 10 percent from the current four percent, the commission said on Monday.

But the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform said it would require government approval for anyone seeking to obtain more than four percent of a bank's stock. Four percent is the current limit.
The proposals would be sent to President Kim Young-sam on Friday, the commission said in a statement.
Financial authorities would evaluate applicants' qualifications, including management ability, credibility and financial status, before approving the expansion, the statement said.
They would also seek to prevent monopolies in the banking system.

The authorities would also monitor how the funds to buy additional stocks were raised and whether the applicant planned a merger or management changes after acquiring more stocks. If an owner failed to meet the government's criteria after acquiring more than four percent of a bank's shares, it would be ordered to reduce its stake to four percent.
The panel said the current 15 percent limit on provincial banks would remain unchanged.
The panel also decided to allow a maximum 10 percent ownership limit on banks newly opened or other financial institutions shifting into banking.

Last week, the panel said it had decided to uphold the four percent ceiling. It added it would propose expanding the ceiling to 10 percent only when banks were newly opened or when other financial institutions shifted into banking.
